title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Rotations, and Templates (v2)
author: Marcus Lee
body:
Purpose and scope:

This playbook defines Redwood Inference's standardized incident lifecycle, runbook conventions, on-call rotation expectations, postmortem requirements, game-day guidance, and communication templates. Use this as the authoritative how-to during incidents and for runbook maintenance.

High-level incident lifecycle:

1) Detect & acknowledge
- Who: PagerDuty -> primary on-call.
- Action: Acknowledge the page within 3 minutes and post a one-line summary to Slack #incidents, then create an incident channel (naming below).

2) Triage & classify
- Assign severity (SEV1-SEV4) using the severity table below.
- If SEV1/SEV2, create a Confluence incident doc from the template, and appoint Incident Commander (IC), Communications Lead, Scribe, and Mitigation Owner.

3) Mitigate
- Execute the relevant runbook. Prioritize safety: stop customer impact first, then diagnose. Capture logs and traces immediately.

4) Restore & verify
- Validate via synthetic checks and dashboards. Coordinate with CS for high-touch customers.

5) Close & learn
- IC runs a hotwash, converts the incident doc into a postmortem (for SEV1/SEV2 within 5 business days), and creates remediation tickets with owners and due dates.

Severity quick reference:
- SEV1: Major outage affecting large proportion of traffic or causing data loss.
- SEV2: Significant degradation for key customer segments or feature.
- SEV3: Single-customer impact or partial degradation with workaround.
- SEV4: Improvements, observations, or low-impact issues.

Escalation matrix:
- 0-10 minutes: Primary responder.
- 10-20 minutes: Escalate to secondary on-call (rotation buddy).
- 20-40 minutes: Paging to SRE manager and service PO.
- 40+ minutes: Engineering Director escalation.

Runbook standards (required fields):
- Name, Owner, Pager rotation, Symptoms, Impact, Pre-reqs (access), Mitigation steps (numbered with commands), Validation, Rollback, Post-incident actions.

Runbook example: GPU-OOM-and-Model-Worker-Flash-Crash
- Owner: eng-serving-runtime (rotation: runtime-oncall)
- Symptoms: sudden spike in pod restarts, node OOM events, GPU memory error logs, >5% request failures in 60s window.
- Pre-reqs: kubectl prod access, node ssh via bastion, grafana dashboard id: runtime-gpu-01.
- Mitigation steps:
  1. Check node status: kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep "NotReady|OutOf"
  2. Inspect pod restarts: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=model-worker -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, restarts:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount}'
  3. If pods are OOMKilled, capture logs: kubectl -n inference logs <pod> --previous > /tmp/<pod>-oom.log
  4. Drain affected node (if GPU kernel issues suspected): kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
  5. Redirect traffic away from heavy models by updating routing config: curl -s -X POST https://admin.internal/api/routing -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' -d '{"model":"gptx-large","action":"deprioritize"}'
  6. Scale up fallback model pool: kubectl -n inference scale deploy model-fallback --replicas=4
- Validation: Confirm model-worker pod error rate <1% for 15 minutes and end-to-end synthetic latency <95p target.
- Post-incident actions: Create JIRA ticket, attach logs, assign to runtime team and model-onboarding for memory profiling.

Postmortem requirements and template:
- Required for all SEV1 and SEV2 incidents within 5 business days. SEV3 reviews at team's discretion.
- Include: title, severity, summary (1 paragraph), timeline (UTC timestamps), root cause, contributing factors, corrective actions (short-term and long-term) with owners and due dates, impact metrics (customers affected, downtime), and lessons learned.

Postmortem template (paste into Confluence):
- Title: Incident: <service> - <brief description> - <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Severity: SEV1/SEV2
- Summary:
  <One-paragraph summary>
- Timeline:
  | Time (UTC) | Actor | Action | Note |
- Root cause:
  <Evidence-backed RCA>
- Remediations:
  * <owner> - <task> - due <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Impact:
  - Customers affected: <count or list>
  - Duration: <minutes>
- Lessons learned and detection/response improvements.

Incident channel naming and Slack templates:
- Naming: #incident-<sev>-YYYYMMDD-HHMM (UTC), e.g. #incident-sev1-20260301-1415
- Initial Slack post (IC or first responder):
  [SEV1] <one-line summary>
  Impact: <who/what>
  Current status: Investigating
  IC: <name> | Scribe: <name> | Comm: <name>
  Channel: #incident-<sev>-YYYYMMDD-HHMM
- Internal status update (every 30 minutes for SEV1):
  - Progress: <short bullets>
  - Next expected update: <time UTC>

Status page & customer communications guidance:
- Publish initial status page entry within 15 minutes of confirmed SEV1/SEV2. Update cadence: 30 minutes for SEV1, hourly for SEV2 until resolved.
- Status page short template:
  Title: Service Degradation - <component> (<YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC>)
  Impact: <summary of who/what>
  Current status: Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Resolved
  Next update: <time UTC>
  Details: <actions>
- High-touch customer email template:
  Subject: Redwood Inference incident affecting <component> on <date>
  Hi <customer>,
  We are investigating an issue affecting <impact>. Current status: <Investigating/Identified/Mitigating>.
  What we are doing: <bulleted mitigations>.
  ETA: <best estimate>.
  Contact: reply to this email or contact your CSM for immediate assistance.

On-call rotations and expectations:
- Rotation cadence: 1-week primary, 2-week secondary.
- Handoff: update rotation spreadsheet and Slack status before end of day on Friday. Include outstanding follow-ups.
- Response expectations: acknowledge pages within 3 minutes, own triage for first 30 minutes, escalate per matrix.
- Training: mandatory shadowing (2 rotations) and attendance at at least one game-day within first 60 days.

Game-day guidance:
- Quarterly team-level, annual platform-level.
- Steps: scenario design (objectives + inject), announce 2 weeks prior, execute in controlled environment, measure detection/mitigation metrics, run debrief within 48 hours, create remediation tickets.

Tooling checklist before mitigation:
- Grafana dashboards, traces (Jaeger/Honeycomb), logs (ES/Datadog), PagerDuty routing, synthetic canaries, admin routing API access.

Evidence retention:
- Preserve incident artifacts (logs, traces, captures) for at least 30 days after SEV1/SEV2. Coordinate with security-and-compliance for customer-sensitive data retention.

Metrics and post-incident tracking:
- Track: MTTR, time-to-detect, number of escalations, action item closure rate.
- Quarterly incident review to identify systemic reliability investments.

Appendix:
A) Contact list and rotation leads: see /team-wiki/oncall-contacts.
B) Runbook index: refer to eng-sre/runbooks-index.
C) Example Confluence incident doc title: "Incident: Model worker OOM storms - 2026-03-01"

Change management:
- To propose updates to this playbook, open a PR to confluence-maintainers and add reviewers from eng-sre and eng-platform. Ensure reviewers include at least one SRE and one runtime engineer.
